query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: A tailored thermo-mechanical treatment—specifically, applying an ~8% cold rolling reduction followed by controlled annealing to produce an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure—will significantly improve the strength, ductility, creep resistance, and corrosion resistance of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy, making it better suited for fasteners under extreme temperature fluctuations and long-term mechanical loads.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar (as-cast) state with balanced but insufficient mechanical performance for industrial fastener applications.
generation.intervention: Tailored thermo-mechanical regimen consisting of cold rolling (~8% reduction) followed by controlled low-temperature annealing designed to initiate recrystallization and phase decomposition.
generation.conditions: Operating environments with extreme temperature fluctuations (up to ~700°C), long-term mechanical loading including room-temperature creep, and exposure to corrosive conditions typical in industrial fastener applications.
generation.structural_mediator: An ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure with enhanced phase boundaries and hierarchical constraints that arrest microcrack propagation.
generation.mechanism: Cold rolling increases dislocation density and introduces plastic deformation defects that serve as nucleation sites during annealing. The controlled annealing promotes recrystallization and phase transformation, yielding an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure that reinforces the alloy via hierarchical constraints. This refined structure is expected to improve dislocation interactions, limit microcrack growth, and enhance resistance to creep and corrosion.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the starting as-cast alloy, the treated alloy would exhibit higher yield and fracture strengths, improved ductility, and enhanced resistance to room-temperature creep and corrosive degradation.
generation.baseline: Uniform, fine lamellar as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy that offers high fracture strength and ductility at room temperature but does not fully meet industrial application requirements under extreme operating conditions.
generation.boundary: Performance improvements are anticipated to be effective under operating temperatures up to approximately 700°C, during long-term mechanical and creep loading tests at room temperature, and in corrosive environments representative of industrial fastener service conditions.
generation.uncertainty: While the enhanced microstructure should improve multiple properties, the precise quantitative gains in creep and corrosion resistance under varied service conditions remain uncertain and may depend on additional environmental factors.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy samples: one set processed via the tailored thermo-mechanical treatment (cold rolling ~8% reduction plus controlled annealing) and a control set in the as-cast, fine lamellar state. Subject both sets to room-temperature and high-temperature (600°C and 700°C) tensile tests, perform room-temperature creep tests using standardized nanoindentation or small-scale uniaxial loading, and conduct accelerated corrosion testing in a corrosive environment representative of industrial fasteners.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated samples do not consistently show statistically significant improvements (e.g., higher strength, greater ductility, lower creep and corrosion rates) relative to the as-cast control samples under the testing conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) can have either high strength or high ductility, and a simultaneous achievement of both still constitutes a tough challenge. The inferior castability and compositional segregation of HEAs are also obstacles for their technological applications. To tackle these problems, here we proposed a novel strategy to design HEAs using the eutectic alloy concept, i.e. to achieve a microstructure composed of alternating soft fcc and hard bcc phases. As a manifestation of this concept, an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 (atomic portion) eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) was designed. The as-cast EHEA possessed a fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure, and showed an unprecedented combination of high tensile ductility and high fracture strength at room temperature. The excellent mechanical properties could be kept up to 700°C. This new alloy design strategy can be readily adapted to large-scale industrial production of HEAs with simultaneous high fracture strength and high ductility.

Realizing improved strength–ductility synergy in eutectic alloys acting as in situ composite materials remains a challenge in conventional eutectic systems, which is why eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs), a newly-emerging multi-principal-element eutectic category, may offer wider in situ composite possibilities. Here, we use an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA to engineer an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure that deliberately inherits its composite lamellar nature by tailored thermo-mechanical processing to achieve property combinations which are not accessible to previously-reported reinforcement methodologies. The as-prepared samples exhibit hierarchically-structural heterogeneity due to phase decomposition, and the improved mechanical response during deformation is attributed to both a two-hierarchical constraint effect and a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism. This work provides a pathway for strengthening eutectic alloys and widens the design toolbox for high-performance materials based upon EHEAs. reading.lever: A tailored thermo-mechanical regimen (cold rolling plus controlled annealing) to generate an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure that enhances hierarchical constraints and arrests microcrack growth.
reading.why: This approach, proven effective in similar eutectic HEAs, directly targets the strength–ductility trade-off while promising improvements in creep and corrosion resistance for fastener applications under extreme conditions.
